title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Five defects in yesterday's own removals
summary: Reading the 1.42.222 diff against a real project rather than against the tests turned up five defects, four of which edit code nothing would have caught.

highlights.title: A refactor that rewrote a string literal
highlights.description: Making a member private looked for the visibility keyword anywhere on the line, so `val label = "make it public "` came back with the string rewritten and the member still public.

highlights.title: A branch emptied in silence
highlights.description: Removing an unheard post could leave an if or else branch with nothing in it. That compiles, so nothing reports it. A post alone in a branch is no longer offered for removal.

highlights.title: Java shells stayed standing
highlights.description: A file left with nothing but its package line was only noticed in Kotlin, because one language check gated two concerns and only one of them is Kotlin specific.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The visibility keyword is read from the leading modifier run, and private lands after the annotations.
A post alone in an if, else, when, for, while, try or catch branch offers no removal; alone in a function body it still does.
A file emptied by a removal is reported in Java as well as in Kotlin.
A name imported twice gives two distinct removals instead of the same one twice.
A dead island counts the tests it removes once, not once per member.
